name: Gibbons Foot and Ankle Group
what_they_do: Solo podiatric practice of Dr. Thomas J. Gibbons doing foot and ankle care including bunions, heel pain, fractures, custom orthotics, ankle instability, diabetic foot issues and foot/ankle surgery. Dr. Gibbons holds surgical privileges at St. Peter's University Hospital, C.A.R.E.S. and Robert Wood Johnson University Hospital.
customers: Adults, many senior and Medicare patients, with foot and ankle pain or surgical needs; referrals from local hospitals and primary care.

size_signals.signal: One doctor with hospital surgical privileges at three named institutions
Long hours, five days a week (Mon to 7:30pm, Wed to 7pm)
Extensive patient-education library (60+ condition articles) and accept-most-insurance messaging

website_review.online_booking_or_quote: None - the office page explicitly says patients must call in advance to reserve time
website_review.trust_signals: Doctor bio page, hospital privileges, Medicare and insurance policy explained, testimonials page, large condition library; review count is low
website_review.out_of_date_signs: Dated template with a fixed 'OUR LOCATION' bar and an accessibility widget crowding the header; section headings clip under the header on mobile; no copyright line found
website_review.search_basics: Title pattern is good ('Office - Podiatrist in East Brunswick, NJ | Gibbons Foot and Ankle Group') and the site has a deep condition/page structure, but there is no schema.org JSON-LD at all and the site initially returned HTTP 403 to a normal browser visit until the user agent was changed
top_issues: No online booking and no contact form - the site tells patients to call, so every booking is a phone call
New-patient paperwork is a downloadable PDF
No schema.org LocalBusiness/Physician markup despite excellent text content (hours, address, insurance, services)
Site blocked a plain browser request with 403 Unauthorized - a fragile setup that can also lock out crawlers

agent_readiness.notes: Findable: crawlable once past the 403 (which is a real risk - the first visit returned '403 Unauthorized'), with hours, address and suite in text. Answerable: hours, insurance, Medicare and appointment policy are written as plain text and would be easy to quote, but there is zero JSON-LD and reviews are thin. Bookable: 0 - no form, no scheduler, and the site explicitly requires a phone call in advance; an agent cannot even leave a request.

operations_signals.signal: New-patient forms must be downloaded as a PDF, printed and brought in - inference: front-desk staff re-key every patient's details
Appointment policy requires calling in advance and says emergencies may cause delays, so the phone line is the single intake channel during a 5-day surgical schedule
Only about a dozen Google reviews exist for a practice with 40+ hours of clinic time a week - inference: no systematic review asking

top_opportunities.opportunity: Add online scheduling or at minimum a labelled appointment-request form, plus digital new-patient intake to replace the PDF
top_opportunities.evidence: New Patients page offers only a PDF download and no form exists anywhere; Office page says patients must call in advance

top_opportunities.opportunity: Add Physician/LocalBusiness JSON-LD and surface reviews on-page; the text content is already strong enough to be quoted by AI agents once it is marked up
top_opportunities.evidence: No script[type=application/ld+json] on any page checked; ~12 reviews against a 7:30pm-closing clinic schedule

top_opportunities.opportunity: Automated appointment reminders and no-show recovery, which matters for a hospital-referral surgical practice where a missed slot is a lost procedure
top_opportunities.evidence: Office page warns that unforeseen emergencies delay the doctor and asks patients to be flexible - inference: schedule churn

scores.reasons: Gap: substantial - no booking, no form, no schema, PDF intake, and a site that 403s normal browser requests. Pay: single practitioner with surgical privileges, so moderate income and a real incentive to fill slots. Ease: scheduling, intake and schema are standard small builds. Evidence: I read the pages and checked for schema myself; the 403 and low review count are directly observed, though review counts come from an aggregator.
